traits_observed: Measured programmatically from the 2048px NB Pro render (masks + min-area-rect analysis). Outer square: axis-aligned, centred, side ~1114px (54% of canvas, generous even margins), drawn as a thin charcoal hairline ~8-17px (~1-1.5% of the mark) with sharp corners. Inner orange square: side ~995px, i.e. about nine tenths (89%) of the outline — far larger than the brief's 'just under three quarters' — concentric with the outline (centroids within 10px of each other) and tilted ~22 degrees instead of the brief's ~11. Because it is so large, ALL FOUR corners overshoot instead of one: each corner crosses a different edge of the outline by ~100px (~9% of the outline side), and the crossings land off-centre along their edges (top edge crossed left of midpoint, right edge above midpoint, bottom edge right of midpoint, left edge below midpoint), giving a calm 4-fold pinwheel rotational symmetry. The orange is flat solid with no outline of its own and sits in front, cleanly interrupting the hairline at each crossing; exactly two colours on pure white. For contrast, the original Recraft rendition of the same direction (job 530980ee) is a loose multi-path SVG with curved bezier edges and broken symmetry — hand-wobbled rather than machined — which is why the NB Pro version won.
